speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; this is a concerning symptom that requires immediate attention. To begin our investigation, how old are you in days, and when did these symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal Malrotation with Volvulus.

The presence of bilious vomiting in a newborn is an absolute surgical emergency, and the family history of a brother with a condition that mimics these symptoms (though pyloric stenosis typically presents with non-bilious vomiting) highlights the urgency. Given the patient's age and symptom onset, I am immediately requesting an Upper GI series to confirm malrotation and rule out volvulus. REQUEST IMAGES: Upper_GI_Series
